I am a poor man in Afar, and the rains here are not kind. My sorghum is what feeds my family, but I have no money for fertilizer from the cooperative, and even if I did, the supply comes too late. I will use the seed I saved from last year like my father did, and my wife and older children will help me with the weeding and watching the birds. If God gives rain, we will eat; if not, we will struggle like always.
